title: Chip Stocks, AI, Fed, Iran, SpaceX
speaker: Kevin Paffrath

macro_themes.view: Expects a US-Iran deal (window Oct 20-27) before the midterms, which would pull yields down and relieve AI funding stress.
10-year peaked near 5.27; needs to come down for neo clouds and IPOs (Anthropic) to proceed.
Hyperscalers keep spending regardless; ~50 GW coming online in 2027 and the next constraint is chips, not data centers.
Expects DRAM prices to start declining next year, good for chip designers and hyperscalers.
Rising mortgage rates hurting entry-level builders; luxury market cash-driven.

calls.reason: Black Monday fears premature; hyperscaler capex, data center build-out and chip shortage support another euphoric rally before an eventual bubble.
calls.quote: I think between now and and then, there's another insane euphoric rally ahead of us.

calls.condition: If an Iran deal comes (window Oct 20-27) and election passes, yields come down; if yields go above the ~5.27 peak, AI trade worsens.
calls.reason: Calls peak 10-year yield ~5.27 already in; Iran deal would quickly ease yields and neo-cloud funding stress.
calls.quote: So far, we did hit peak yields, which we talked about peak being about 527-ish

calls.condition: Neo clouds require an Iran deal to lower funding costs; without it they keep suffering.
calls.reason: CDS spiking in a doom loop of stock, bonds and CDS; most rate-sensitive, debt-funded build-out.
calls.quote: the neo clouds basically are untouchable with uh an Iran deal... these guys require Iran deal

calls.reason: Oracle CDS 'to the moon' (~300); pain not over though balance sheet better than CoreWeave.
calls.quote: Yeah, dude. Oracle's like 300 now. Oh my gosh. Yeah, this pain ain't over yet.

calls.reason: ~23x forward P/E with ~35% growth, PEG ~0.65; silicon shortage and lower RAM per GPU benefit Nvidia.
calls.quote: Nvidia is trading for a 0.65 PEG ratio right now.

calls.reason: Contract liabilities jumped from 3.5B to 9.3B EUR, signalling booming machine orders ahead of a chip shortage; ~36x P/E with ~25% growth.
calls.quote: that's actually pretty bullish even for the Nvidia build out or just really any of the chips

calls.reason: Chip plays at discounts; nearly bounced on his 520 line; bleeding-edge chips benefit from stabilising memory prices.
calls.quote: it kind of reiterates how it just feels like you're you've got this opportunity in in these discounts

notes: Live stream on a Monday ('this weekend' black Monday fears, New Arab report 'on Monday'), so dated 2026-10-19; listing approx_date 2026-10-20. video_type set to macro_interview (no guest; host macro commentary).
